hero.title: Presentation, Projects, and Research
hero.subtitle: I am a 4th-year student at École Polytechnique, following a curriculum that merges mathematics and computer science. While art and science are often seen as opposites, I consider them inseparable: science allows us to understand the world, while art allows us to feel it. To me, combining analytical rigor with intuition and artistic sensitivity is essential. My affinity for the arts is expressed through music—playing several instruments and composing—as well as through visual arts and literature, particularly poetry. However, while this sensitivity fuels my reflection, it never compromises my scientific standards. This duality shapes my philosophy of life and research: maintaining absolute attention to the rigor of every assertion I make.
hero.artwork_desc: Rythme n°1 (1938) by Robert Delaunay. This monumental composition marks the pinnacle of the artist's research into Orphism and simultaneous contrast. Through concentric circles and curves, Delaunay explores the pure dynamics of color, creating an illusion of movement solely through the physical interaction of the viewer's gaze.
hero.monet_artwork_desc: The House Seen from the Rose Garden (c. 1922-1924) by Claude Monet. In this late work, Monet moves away from faithful representation to capture a pure impression. Contours fade in favor of a chromatic burst, foreshadowing lyrical abstraction through a vibrant study of light.
hero.poem_intro:
Like a shrill flight of birds in a flurry,
All my memories fall upon me,
hero.poem_rest:
Fall amidst the yellow foliage
Of my heart mirroring its bent alder trunk
In the violet sheen of the water of Regrets,
Which flows melancholy nearby,
Fall, and then the evil rumor
That a moist breeze, rising, soothes,
Dies out by degrees in the tree, so well
That after a moment nothing more is heard,
Nothing more but the voice celebrating the Absent One,
Nothing more but the voice—oh, so languid!—
Of the bird that was my First Love,
And which still sings as on the first day;
And, in the sad splendor of a moon
Rising pale and solemn, a
Melancholy and heavy summer night,
Full of silence and darkness,
Cradles on the azure that a soft wind grazes
The shivering tree and the weeping bird.

publications.title: ToxiFrench: Benchmarking and Enhancing Language Models via CoT Fine-Tuning for French Toxicity Detection
publications.logo_desc: Research conducted in collaboration with SJTU University.
publications.meta: Axel Delaval, Shujian Yang, Haicheng Wang, Han Qiu, Jialiang Lu - Shanghai Jiao Tong University (SJTU) - 2025
publications.desc: French toxicity detection suffers from a lack of annotated data. We present ToxiFrench, a dataset of 53,622 comments built via an innovative semi-automated pipeline. Our research reveals that smaller models (SLMs) often surpass giant models in robustness. To leverage this potential, we introduce a Chain-of-Thought (CoT) fine-tuning strategy with Dynamic Weighted Loss (DWL). Our optimized Qwen3-4B model outperforms GPT-4o and DeepSeek-R1, setting a new state-of-the-art while preserving its multilingual capabilities.

chips.desc: Natural Language Processing.

projects.title: EULAI: Local AI Assistant for Legal Document Analysis (January 2026)
projects.logo_desc: EULAI: Browser extension for analyzing ToS and privacy policies.
projects.desc:
EULAI is a privacy-centric Chrome extension that summarizes and analyzes complex legal documents (ToS, Privacy Policies) directly in the browser. It is one of the first extensions to leverage 100% local inference via WebGPU.

• Local Inference: High-performance AI chat powered by MLC Web-LLM (fine-tuned Qwen-0.6B model).
• Hierarchical Segmentation: Intelligent processing of massive documents to prevent context loss.
• Source Transparency: 'View Source' feature showing the exact segment used by the AI.
• TOS;DR Style Outputs: Clause classification into [GOOD], [NEUTRAL], [BAD], and [BLOCKER].

chips.desc: Running LLMs locally within the browser.
